method: Look-through composites from each company's own SEC filings (XBRL companyfacts, parsed by fundamentals.py). A fund with weight w in a company of market value mcap owns w/mcap of it; every measure is the sum of those owned slices of a numerator over the same of a denominator. P/E = sum(w) / sum(w x earnings / mcap), the weighted harmonic mean, losses included ('aggregate loss' when the sum is not positive). EV measures and margins over operating companies only (banks and insurers: P/E, P/B, dividend yield). Growth holds today's ownership fixed: sum(w x X now / mcap) / sum(w x X a year earlier / mcap) - 1. Trailing twelve months, GAAP, as filed; statements converted to US dollars at the run's FX; market value = last close x latest filed share count (per ADR for an ADR); companies aggregated by CIK. Covered = a US listing in SEC's ticker map whose company has usable SEC figures ending no more than 200 days ago, a last close and an FX rate. A composite is shown only when covered companies make up at least 70 pct of the row's weight. A company is left out (uncovered, with its reason) when its latest whole-company share count is dated more than 400 days before its latest quarter, or when the market value it implies is implausible against its own filings (under 0.5 pct of revenue or 3 pct of equity, earnings above 5x or dividends above 1x the value). Ratios to the market (SPY) are published only when SPY's own composite is shown and inside a sane band (P/E 10-45x, dividend yield 0.5-4 pct, EV/sales 0.8-6x); otherwise each reads not available with the reason. No analyst estimates or revisions: there is no free source. A fund's own published figures use other definitions (vendor earnings, losses often excluded) and are a cross-check, not this number.
